name: sdk-py
what_it_holds: Official MIT-licensed Python client (27 stars, 341 commits, updated 5 May 2026) for the PredictHQ Events/Demand-Intelligence API. Endpoints: Events (concerts, festivals, sports, conferences, public + school holidays, severe weather, term/academic dates, community events, disasters) globally, ranked by predicted attendance/impact; Places; Features (pre-aggregated demand-forecast features by location/date, e.g. a 'PHQ Rank' or attendance sum per day per area); Broadcasts (TV viewership tied to events); polygon/radius impact-area queries. This is the exact event-demand feed that vacation-rental dynamic-pricing engines (PriceLabs, Wheelhouse, Beyond Pricing all cite PredictHQ as a data partner) plug into to move nightly rates around demand shocks. No data files are committed; it is a live-API pull (free tier exists but usage-limited).
why_useful: Standard, well-documented client for pulling a global multi-category event calendar (concerts/conferences/sports) with impact/attendance scores by location -- the general-purpose tool for the whole 'events and shocks' gap (#11), not just World Cup. Method only, not a dataset; a human would need to register for a key.
time_coverage: current + forward-looking via API (no vintage/historical bulk export)
themes: Event calendars: FIFA World Cup 2026 schedule and host-city data, Olympics, concerts (Setlist.fm, Songkick, Ticketmaster API), conferences, PredictHQ samples, holiday calendars by country
Corporate travel and business-travel data (GBTA, Concur/SAP, Navan public indices, conference calendars), MICE datasets

why_all: Standard, well-documented client for pulling a global multi-category event calendar (concerts/conferences/sports) with impact/attendance scores by location -- the general-purpose tool for the whole 'events and shocks' gap (#11), not just World Cup. Method only, not a dataset; a human would need to register for a key.

Would be the mechanical route to a global events-and-impact feed (concerts, conferences, sports, public holidays, severe weather) PredictHQ sells, matching the 'PredictHQ samples' keyword in the theme, but is gated behind a paid API key that the project rules say not to use (no paid keys) — catalogued as a method only, not actionable without a licence.

Fills gap #11 (events and shocks) and the MICE/conference-calendar keyword directly -- a per-city, per-week conference/expo signal is exactly the kind of business-travel demand proxy the theme is chasing, though it is a paid-tiered acquisition method rather than a free static dataset.

Maps directly onto CONTEXT.md gap #11 (events/shocks: FIFA World Cup 2026, concerts, conferences) and #17 (event-study/nowcasting methods). A PredictHQ 'Features' pull by market (NA/EMEA/LatAm/APAC metros) around the 3Q26 World Cup window or major-market festival calendars could be turned into an independent, point-in-time event-density regressor for nights/ADR that is not derived from Airbnb data itself.

name: disasters (Measuring Economic Disruption from Climate Disasters)
what_it_holds: Replication package for paper measuring selection into the EM-DAT disaster record against MODIS burned-area and IBTrACS (hurricane) wind-field data. Repo holds bundled data as split archives (Climate_damage_full.bundle.part00/01, Climate_damage_repo.tar.gz.part00/01) plus code; README describes a 1,174-row register linking every number in the paper to its source (EM-DAT entry, MODIS burned area, IBTrACS wind fields, separating entry/monetisation/magnitude margins). No stars yet, updated 24 Aug 2026.
why_useful: Directly usable for gap 11 (hurricanes/wildfires as tourism shocks) and gap 17 (methods/event-study/replication packages): gives a rigorous, sourced EM-DAT-vs-satellite cross-walk that could be adapted to flag disaster severity for ABNB-relevant markets (Maui, LA, Gulf Coast, Caribbean) rather than relying on raw EM-DAT counts alone.
size_hint: multi-part bundle + tar.gz archives (exact size unknown, split into parts suggesting >100MB)
time_coverage: not fully specified; EM-DAT/IBTrACS/MODIS overlap era (~2000s-2020s)

why_all: Directly usable for gap 11 (hurricanes/wildfires as tourism shocks) and gap 17 (methods/event-study/replication packages): gives a rigorous, sourced EM-DAT-vs-satellite cross-walk that could be adapted to flag disaster severity for ABNB-relevant markets (Maui, LA, Gulf Coast, Caribbean) rather than relying on raw EM-DAT counts alone.

A ready-made, point-in-time-conscious linkage of EM-DAT (global disaster event records: type, country, date, deaths, damages) to MODIS/IBTrACS -- gives the team a vetted way to pull EM-DAT-quality disaster events (wildfires, storms, floods) by country/date for building an events-and-shocks regressor without re-deriving the EM-DAT extract from scratch, and models exactly the kind of selection/measurement bias (what gets recorded vs. not) that matters if disaster counts are used as a KPI driver.
